title: Layer-misplacement failure: how badly does steering at the wrong layer backfire?

original_idea.body: Layer-misplacement failure: sweep a steering vector across every layer, measure penalty for mis-layering. Inference-only on open models.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: layer-sensitivity guidance improves steering reliability, but catastrophic-risk link is a step removed (level 3).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Layer sweep with matched norm is a clear inherited methodology; novice+mentor feasible (level 4).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (per-layer sensitivity map), two-model comparison adds modest scope (level 4).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Some externally-doable practical-guidance slice, but layer-sweeps are common; mixed (level 3).

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only sweep on open models, single GPU (level 4).

novelty.reasoning: Layer-dependence well known; systematic mis-layering penalty per concept may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Layer-sensitivity is studied; a penalty-focused per-concept map may be open.
